findings.claim: The generated resolver part now always carries `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, and that attribute has AllowMultiple=false. A user who already applied it to their resolver gets a compile error (CS0579 duplicate attribute) in the generated file. Example: `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver][ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] partial class MyResolver {}`. Applying it by hand is the obvious pre-existing workaround for this exact issue. The template adds the attribute without checking whether the user's partial declaration already has it, so these projects stop building. The same applies to `[CompositeResolver]` partial classes in CompositeResolverTemplate.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageDuplicateTests.UserAppliedExcludeFromCodeCoverageOnResolverDoesNotBreakBuild. It passes on base and fails on head with an unexpected CS0579 in MyNs.MyResolver.g.cs.

findings.claim: The `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard drops the attribute for projects targeting netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists on both (.NET Framework 4.0+ and netstandard2.0, with Class targets allowed). The guard is therefore unnecessary, and generated formatters and resolvers in those projects remain counted in coverage. This contradicts "all generated code is decorated". The acceptance criteria allow conditional emission only where the attribute does not exist.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator with CSharpParseOptions preprocessor symbols NETSTANDARD2_0 (or NETFRAMEWORK) against netstandard2.0 reference assemblies. Assert that the generated formatter type's GetAttributes() contains ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. On head it is absent, although removing the #if still compiles against netstandard2.0.
